title: FLORA POLICE ARREST
full_story:
The Flora Police Department announced that, as a result of an ongoing investigation, an additional charge has been filed against Rodney J. Greenwood.

Flora police determined that between January 1st, 2024, and March 1st, 2026, Greenwood was in Possession of Child Sexual Abuse Material, in violation of Illinois statute 720 ILCS 5/11-20.1(a)(7).

In cooperation with Clay County State’s Attorney, Phillip Givens, formal charges were filed in Clay County Court yesterday, for the aforementioned statute.

Greenwood was remanded to the custody of the Clay County Jail as the Judge found he should continue to be detained.

All subjects are presumed innocent until proven guilty in a court of law.

title: STUDENTS FOUND SAFE
full_story:
The Marion County Sheriff’s Department was contacted by the Iuka School on Wednesday concerning 3 students who left the school grounds without authorization.

School officials reported to the Iuka Police and Marion County Sheriff that the students were observed running from an outdoor physical Education class.  Law enforcement promptly coordinated a search effort.  The students had entered a heavily wooded area near the school, and the search included a drone and helicopter.

All three students were located unharmed and have been reunited with their families.

title: IECC BOARD MEETING
full_story:
The Board of Trustees of the Illinois Eastern Community College District met Tuesday night at Frontier Community College, in Fairfield.

The Board approved honoring Jerry Cox’s longstanding support of IECC by naming the new Frontier Community College athletic facility the Jerry Cox Athletic Center and its competition floor the Jerry Cox Court, recognizing his significant donations and ongoing commitment to student success.

The Board approved fee updates effective Fall 2026, including the elimination testing fee which will save students approximately $177, and redistributing a $40 lab fee in the Medical Assistant program evenly across two courses without changing total program cost.

A new three-year agreement with Assessment Technologies Institute (ATI) to continue providing nursing students with testing, remediation, and NCLEX preparation through a cost-recovery fee assessed to first-year RN students was approved.

Approval of employment was given for Adam McInter as TRIO Upward Bound Academic Counselor at LTC effective June 1st, 2026 and Vanessa Stevens as OCC Custodian effective April 27th.

New employment contracts were approved for Chancellor Ryan Gower; LTC President/Vice Chancellor of Institutional Outreach Tona Ambrose; OCC President/Vice Chancellor of Business Operations Chris Simpson; and FCC President/Vice Chancellor of Business & Industry Sharmila Kakac.  Retirement ratification was approved for Dr. Matthew Fowler as WVC President and Vice Chancellor of Student Affairs effective June 30, 2027.

The next regular meeting of the Board of Trustees will be Tuesday, May 19th, at Lincoln Trail College, in Robinson.

title: CEO TRADE SHOW
full_story:
The Clay County CEO (Creating Entrepreneurial Opportunities) Class of 2026 will host its annual Trade Show on Wednesday, from 5:00 to 7:00 PM at the New Beginnings Church in Flora, where nine student entrepreneurs will showcase the individual businesses, they have developed throughout the school year.

The trade show represents the culmination of a year-long experience in which students learn the fundamentals of business by creating and operating their own ventures.  Community members are invited to attend, meet the students, and explore a wide variety of products and services created by local high school seniors.

Andrew Shelby, owner of HydroHoops, offers custom hydrodipped basketballs that feature unique, eye-catching designs, helping players easily identify their ball while expressing personal style.

Carder Walden created G2G (Glory to God), a Christian bracelet brand featuring high-quality woven bracelets with Bible verses printed on the inside, designed to inspire faith and spark meaningful conversations.

Chloe Whitmire, owner of Chloe’s Cleaning Co., provides residential and commercial cleaning services focused on reliability, attention to detail, and creating clean, welcoming environments.

Ella Cammon operates Essentials by Ella, a business that designs and sells organized, easy-to-use emergency car kits aimed at helping drivers feel safe and prepared for unexpected situations.

Halle Kitley brings creativity to the forefront with Patched Hat Bar, where customers can design their own custom trucker hats using a variety of patches and styles.

Haven Cash founded The Growing Point, a gardening brand offering curated boxes with seeds, guidance, and resources to help individuals and families learn and succeed in gardening.

Mason Byers, owner of Better Bites, produces protein balls and healthy snacks made with quality ingredients, offering a convenient and nutritious option for busy lifestyles.

Noah Hatcher created Fore You Golf, a custom golf accessory brand that allows golfers to personalize items such as balls, tees, markers, and towels.

Parker Helm launched LATHR, a men’s grooming brand specializing in high-quality scented soap bars designed to deliver premium fragrances and a refined grooming experience.

The Clay County CEO program emphasizes real-world learning by connecting students with local business leaders, providing mentorship opportunities, and allowing students to experience entrepreneurship firsthand.  The Trade Show serves as a final opportunity for students to present their work, engage with customers, and put their skills into action.

Community members are encouraged to attend and support these young entrepreneurs as they take an important step toward their futures in business and beyond.

title: FLORA FFA PLANT SALE
full_story:

title: 5th ANNUAL MASONIC AUCTION
full_story:
The 5th Annual Flora Masonic Lodge Auction will take place Saturday, May 30th at 10:00 am at the Clay County Fairgrounds in Charley Brown Park.

Anyone can donate, to make a donation call 618-843-3815.  Checks and money orders should be made out to the Shriners Hospital and mailed to Don Fry at 323 East 4th Street in Flora.  Donations will be accepted within a 50-mile radius of Flora.  The auction flyer also contains a QR Code that can be scanned to make a donation directly to the Shriner’s Hospital.  The auction never fails to offer many useful and intriguing items.  Dagg’s Auction Service will be the auctioneer.

title: FREEDOM CAUCUS PRIORITIES
full_story:
Instead of focusing on property taxes, affordable energy and improving student proficiencies, the Democratic-controlled Legislature continues to churn out one terrible bill after another and ignore the needs of working people, according to the Illinois Freedom Caucus.

“When you stack up the ridiculous legislation that the Democrats have passed so far this Spring against the actual reform-minded ideas that have not even been assigned to committee, the priorities of the radical left become pretty clear,” said State Representative Chris Miller.  “It is obvious that the Democrats, who have had one party rule for the majority of this century, are the ones who have destroyed Illinois through bad public policy.  And yet, they still believe the answer is more legislation, more regulation, more government, more taxes, more mandates.”

One area of concern is the money being spent on the failed Commission on Equity and Inclusion.

“The Commission on Equity and Inclusion has spent approximately $15 Million dollars since its inception, and they are asking for another 5.7 million this year,” said State Representative Brad Halbrook.  “At the same time, they have erased half the state’s vendors from their program due to failed oversight and planning by their leadership.  And speaking of that leadership, after their worst year, the commission has ever had, they want an 8% increase in the salaries of all their executives.  Remember, these are taxpayer funded salaries.  If performance measures compensation, these people need a pay cut, not a raise.”

State Representative Adam Niemerg said the misguided priorities are not only wasting time on the House Floor and in Committees but are also doing tremendous harm to the people of the state.

“The intent behind these far-left initiatives is not to make life in Illinois better,” said State Representative Adam Niemerg.  “The intent is to use the law to make political statements.  Voters in our state did not send us here to Springfield to make political statements.  We were sent here to solve problems and put the interests of our citizens first.  These far-left policies the Democrats are pushing won’t help lower utility bills, won’t make our communities safe, and won’t lower skyrocketing property taxes.”

State Representative Blaine Wilhour said it is time to stop focusing on trivial matters and get serious about the issues important to Illinois citizens.

“We could be addressing out of control electric bills.  We could be making changes to the SAFE-T Act to ensure violent offenders are not roaming our streets,” Wilhour said.  “We could be focused on a host of issues of great concern to our constituents.  But the message the Democrats send every day is they do not work for the people.  They work for the funders of their campaigns.  And as long as this corrupt system remains in place, we will continue to see bad bill after bad bill fly through both chambers while the real issues voters care about continue to be ignored.  There is a reason why Illinois continues to lose population.  The people are voting with their feet because they are sick and tired of the unserious people running our state. ”

title: STATE UPGRADES RESERVATION SYSTEM
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Natural Resources (IDNR) is upgrading the reservation system for campgrounds and shelters at Illinois State Parks.  IDNR officials say the new system will offer a more user-friendly experience while making reservations and securing permits.

One change to the system will include the opportunity to book shelter reservations up to 12 months in advance, instead of waiting until July 1st to make reservations.  Users will continue to use exploremoreil.com to make campsite and shelter reservations.

To ease the transition, electronic reservations will not be available April 27th through 30th.  Customers will still be able to make walk-up reservations at campgrounds during that time.  Anyone with an existing reservation will be able to keep their reservation, but all customers will need to create a new account and password in the new system.  Users will be able to use the same email to access their reservation.

Existing customers should watch their inbox for an email from IDNR with further instructions.

title: IHSA COMMITTEE MEETS
full_story:
The Illinois High School Association (IHSA) has established a competitive balance committee, which aims to address disparities between public and private schools competing in interscholastic athletics.  The committee has already met twice.

IHSA Executive Director Craig Anderson says the committee will meet monthly through September and look at the association’s multiplier, success factor, and 30-mile radius that non-boundaried schools can pull students from.

The IHSA competitive balance committee is made up of eight public school administrators, six private school administrators, and three IHSA administrators.
